Subject: Acme POC kickoff recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the kickoff today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Pain & goals (confirmed)
- Pain: High per-token cost and unpredictable latency on customer-facing search/chat flows; frequent tail-latency spikes during peak traffic.
- Goal: Reduce median response latency to <350ms for 1k QPS baseline and target 30% cost reduction vs current infra within POC window, without degrading relevance.

POC scope (what we agreed)
- Inference targets: 3 representative endpoints (search ranking, conversational assistant, summarization).
- Models: open-llm-family LLM v2 (quantized variant) for generation; Redwood Optimize heuristics for batching & caching.
- Duration: 6 weeks (Feb 8 -> Mar 21) with a mid-point review (week 3).
- Success metrics: latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec cost, and retrieval+LLM relevance (precision@5 on the prompt set).

Owners & access
- Acme: Alice (technical lead) — will provide test dataset, API keys for telemetry, and a staging environment. Procurement will handle contract signature.
- Redwood: Marissa (eng sponsor), Aditya (onboarding / infra), Rishi (SE — prompts, evals, tuning).

Immediate next steps (by Feb 5)
1) Alice: share a 1-2 GB anonymized sample dataset and service account for staging access.
2) Acme procurement: sign the SOW / purchase order (we already shared the DocuSign).
3) Redwood (Aditya + Rishi): send the POC runbook and access checklist; schedule environment setup call for Feb 8.

Attachments: I attached the POC plan and the access checklist we referenced.

If I missed anything, flag it and I will update. Otherwise we’ll assume these action owners/timelines and kick off next Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we can share a 1.5 GB anonymized dump of recent search queries + doc corpus by Friday (Feb 5). Will include a simple schema and mapping notes.
- Staging access: we’ll provision a service account and VPN access (no production data). Expect to send creds to Aditya by EOD Feb 5.
- Success metrics: procurement wants a short success definition for contract sign-off. For us, the key is 30% lower per-token cost at equivalent or better relevance, and p95 latency <700ms during simulated peak traffic.

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple technical notes so the Feb 8 environment setup call goes smoothly: 

- Access checklist: we typically need a staging service account with read access to the test dataset and a temporary API token for telemetry ingestion. The acme-access-checklist.xlsx attached outlines exact ports and CIDR ranges for our staging instances.
- Prompt set & evals: could you include 50 representative prompts for each endpoint (search, chat, summarization)? We’ll run an automatic relevance eval (precision@5) and share the eval harness.
- Traffic profile: please indicate expected QPS and an example peak window so we can pre-warm KV caches and configure batching.

I’ll post a runbook and the initial prompt templates by EOD Feb 4. We’ll aim to have a baseline run by Feb 12 so we can iterate during the first two weeks.
